Informant PW.1 in his cross-examination admitted that there was a boundary between his house and those of the accused and a civil suit was pending on the boundary issue. A partition suit was also pending between the parties, he admitted. Informant also admitted that he initiated a proceeding under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the accused on the disputed pathway. PW. 1 admitted that appellants Imam and Rafique are the sons of appellant Motaleb who is an old aged man. He also admitted that appellant Polash is the nephew of Motaleb and accused Biplob is the son of dead accused Anwar. PW.2 Habibur Rahman who hails from the same village claimed that on hearing alarm he rushed to the spot. This PW stated about the assault on the informant and dragging him to a khal by Motaleb, Rafique, Imam and Biplob. He did not speak about any demand of subscription and/or donation by any of the accused persons. This PW admitted that the accused persons are the neighbours of the informant. PW.3 Ajmol Hossain, a cousin of the informant, who came at the relevant time on a visit to the house of the informant, deposed about the assault on Kajal Begum, wife of the informant. This PW quoted Kajal Begum and claimed that for the refusal to give subscription the accused persons assaulted her. The PW.3 further deposed that he heard about the attack on the informant as he refused to pay subscription. But in his cross-examination he admitted that did not hear about the demand of subscription. PW.4 the Kajal Begum is the wife of informant. She deposed about the assault on her when she prevented Motaleb, Palash, Imam and Biplob who were after her husband. She claimed that appellant Polash gave her lathi blows, undressed sari from her body and thereby caused outrage of her modesty; appellant Imam took away a gold chain of eight annas in weight from her neck. This PW did not say a single word about demand of subscription and/or putting in fear herself or her husband to give any subscription. She admitted that her husband initiated a proceeding under section 144 of Code of Criminal Procedure that was ultimately dismissed. PW.5 Abdur Razzak Khan, a teacher of Amirabad High School, in his evidences stated about the assault on informant near the house of Wazed Ali and dragging him to a khal by Motaleb, Anwar, Biplob and Imam. This PW claimed that he prevented the accused from such act and sent the informant to his house. This PW also did not speak about any demand of subscription. PW.6 Joynal Hossain Majhi, also a cousin of informant, stated that accused Motaleb, Imam, Rafique, Polash and Biplob gave assault on informant and his wife and after demanding subscription they snatched away a gold chain from Kajal Begum. In his cross-examination he told that lead about the demand of subscription from the informant and his wife. Investigating officer PW.7 SI Abdus Salam found in his investigation that the informant and the accused are the neighbours. He admitted that he did not collect any direct evidence about the demand of subscription though he denied the suggestion that he did not go to the place of occurrence for investigation. 

 14. Let us now proceed with the 'question' whether the prosecution is able to prove that the appellants put in fear the informant and/his wife in fear, or attempted to put in fear any of them, of any injury in order to commit extortion. On this aspect of the matter the only evidence, as we have already noticed, of PW.1, the informant. It has to be remembered that PW.1 is the man who was silent in his deposition before the Tribunal about demand of subscription for the construction of a pathway and his promise to pay putting in fear in the previous occasion as he claimed in the FIR. He only, in his deposition, implicated absconding accused Biplob in demanding and threatening him for subscription of taka twenty five thousand. This is not supported by any of the other PWs. Furthermore, PW.4 Kajal Begum did not corroborate his husband about the demand of subscription. Of course, PWs. 2, 3, 5, and 6 spoke about the assault on the informant and dragging him to a khal, assault on his wife after entering in her residence and taking away of her gold chain, for those the appellants were put on trial separately. But any of them did not speak directly about any demand of subscription and/or donation by any of the accused persons and having been refused they did those acts. Although P.W.3 quoted Kajal Begum and claimed that for the refusal to give subscription the accused persons assaulted but Kajal Begum herself did not speak so. The evidence of P.W.6 in this regards also hearsay. Moreover P.W.7 investigating officer admitted that he did not collect any direct evidence about the demand of subscription. We found no body except P.W.1 to come with the case that the appellants assaulted the informant and her wife on refusal to give subscription demanded by them. Admittedly appellants Imam and Rafique are the sons of appellant Motaleb who is an old aged man and appellant Polash is the nephew of Motaleb and absconding accused Biplob is the son of deceased accused Anwar. Common boundary between his houses of the parties, pendency of civil suits in particular for partition and unsuccessful proceedings by the informant under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the disputed pathway against the accused appellants are the admitted facts. In view of this, it is not safe to take all that PW.1 said as truth. We find no legal evidence as regards the demand of subscription of taka twenty five thousand. In the above circumstances it is not safe to rely on the sole testimony of PW.1 without corroboration from any other independent evidence to show intention of the appellants for extorting delivery of subscription of taka twenty five thousand as claimed by the prosecution. In absence of any credible and legal evidence, which may indicate that the appellants put in fear the informant and/or his wife with intention of extorting delivery of such subscription, we are constrained to hold that the prosecution has failed to prove a case under section 385 of the Penal Code against the appellants. As such we see merit in the appeal.
